summary: All parts of the request (nearest-rank formula, p validation, empty list, input immutability, five example values) are covered by three atomic requirements with concrete acceptance criteria. No blocking problems; a few minor precision and testability gaps are noted.

checklist.item: Every part of the request covered
checklist.note: Formula, p range/non-integer, empty list, immutability and the five examples map to REQ-001..003 and AC-001-1..5.
REQ-003 has no acceptance criteria; p=50.0 handling is not explicit (see F-1, F-2).
Concrete inputs and expected outputs; AC-001-6 is less specific but acceptable.
Immutability constraint and assumptions on input type and size are recorded.
Pairwise review performed; no real conflicts exist.
No security or data-loss decisions; open_issues empty.
ASM-001 bool rejection is sensible; ASM-002 leaves NaN or non-numeric behaviour undefined.

findings.description: REQ-003 (input list unchanged) has no acceptance criterion, so there is no measurable pass condition. Add e.g. 'after percentile([50,15,40], 50) the list is still [50,15,40]'.
REQ-002 does not say whether integral floats such as p=50.0 are rejected. 'Not an integer' is ambiguous; AC-002-2 only covers 50.5. State it explicitly.

The formula r = ceil(p/100 x N) is vulnerable to floating-point error with float arithmetic (e.g. exact products landing slightly above an integer). Require exact integer arithmetic, i.e. ceil(p*N/100) = (p*N+99)//100, or add a boundary AC.
Behaviour for NaN or non-numeric scores is undefined (ASM-002); acceptable but worth noting.
